market.question: Will Crude Oil (CL) hit (HIGH) $175 by end of June?

assessment.reasoning: WTI front-month (CLM26) is currently trading around $94/bbl as of April 25, 2026 — approximately 80% below the $175 target, requiring an ~86% rally in roughly 9 weeks. The geopolitical context is already highly elevated: the Strait of Hormuz is essentially closed, a US naval blockade on Iran is in place, and WTI already surged ~70% from pre-conflict levels to a 52-week high of $117.63. The EIA STEO expects Brent to peak near $115/b in Q2 2026 before easing, implying WTI (which trades at roughly a $10–12 discount to Brent) peaks near $103–105 — well short of $175. Even the most bullish analyst scenarios (LiteFinance upper band of $137 for 2026) fall far short of $175. Reaching $175 would require a catastrophic supply shock beyond current disruptions — e.g., complete and irreversible Persian Gulf shut-in plus secondary supply failures. The 52-week high is $117.63, meaning $175 would represent an all-time record by a wide margin. Tail-risk scenario probability (escalation, second front, pipeline sabotage) is real but low — estimated at ~10–12%.
data_sources: OilPrice.com / Trading Economics: WTI front-month ~$94.40 as of Apr 25, 2026
EIA STEO April 2026: Brent to peak ~$115/b in Q2 2026
Barchart CLM26: June WTI closed ~$94–95 range week of Apr 21-25
LiteFinance bullish 2026 WTI forecast: $111.54–$137.30 upper range
IEA Oil Market Report March 2026: US-Israel air strikes on Iran began Feb 28, Strait of Hormuz largely closed
Reuters poll Feb 2026: WTI average forecast $60.38/bbl for full year 2026
assessment.key_uncertainty: Whether the US-Iran conflict dramatically escalates (e.g., full Persian Gulf production shutoff, attacks on Saudi/UAE infrastructure) — the single scenario that could drive WTI toward $150+ territory, though even that scenario likely falls short of $175 CME settlement.
